facts.text: Bowling Green earned its name when a regional postal carrier, fond of his Kentucky hometown, christened the settlement in 1832.
The late 19‑century discovery of oil sparked a boom that still echoes in the grand downtown storefronts along Wooster Street.
Bowling Green State University, founded in 1910, is the city’s beating heart and hosts the nationally recognized National Tractor Pulling Championships each August.
Every September, the Black Swamp Arts Festival turns the city into a canvas of murals, music, and local crafts, drawing visitors from across the region.
Wood County Heritage Days, held annually, showcases vintage tractors, gas engines, and living‑history reenactors, celebrating the area’s agricultural roots.
The 1890s Neoclassical courthouse, a landmark of civic pride, stands on the square where the city first became the county seat in 1868.
